bugs.name: Exclusive label Priority/Low cannot be found by its complete saved name in issue Labels filter
bugs.summary: In the issue sidebar's Labels menu, typing the complete saved name of the existing exclusive label "Priority/Low" removes the label from the list and shows "No results found."
bugs.expected: Filtering by the label's exact saved name "Priority/Low" should keep that label in the menu so it can be selected.
bugs.actual: The menu shows "No results found." and the Priority/Low label cannot be selected through the filter.
reproSteps: Use the saved session for the disposable fixture admin account (eval).
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/labels and confirm that the exclusive label Priority/Low exists (it is shown as a split 'Priority | Low' badge).
Click the gear next to Labels in the right sidebar.
Type Priority/Low into the Filter Label box.
bugs.reason: User rejected this claim after checking that both scope and value can be searched together. The picker searches rendered text with the scope and value concatenated: for the exclusive label foo/foo1, foo, foo1 and foofoo1 all find it. The literal slash query foo/foo1 and space query foo foo1 do not match. The reported full-name miss is real, but a requirement to normalize slash/space separators is not established; it is not a failure to search both components. Reject this exact separator-formatting claim, not a report where scope, value or the concatenated text actually fails.

bugs.name: Label template dropdown partially obscures Advanced option text behind the selection control
bugs.summary: The report claims the empty Labels page's label-set dropdown renders the Advanced option underneath the selection control on mobile, leaving only its trailing text visible.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects both label sets to be fully visible when the dropdown opens.
bugs.actual: At phone width the menu opens showing only the end of the Advanced option above the selected Default option.
reproSteps: Open the Labels page of an organization or repository that has no labels, at a 390px-wide viewport.
Open the label-set dropdown and observe only the end of the Advanced option is visible at the top.
bugs.reason: Intended dropdown behavior, not overlap: on mobile the menu is a short scrollable box (Fomantic caps its height at small widths) that opens scrolled to the selected Default option. Advanced sits above the visible area, scrolling up shows it in full, and it can be selected. Both options are fully visible on desktop.

bugs.name: Renaming an exclusive label to a name without a scope clears Exclusive
bugs.summary: The report claims that renaming an exclusive label such as 'x/y' to a plain name such as 'z' wrongly removes its Exclusive setting.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the label to stay exclusive after being renamed to 'z'.
bugs.actual: After renaming 'x/y' to 'z' and saving, the label is no longer exclusive and the Exclusive checkbox is disabled.
reproSteps: Replace the whole name with 'z' and save.
Reopen the label and observe Exclusive is unchecked.
bugs.reason: Intended: only scoped labels (names with a 'scope/' prefix) can be exclusive, so the dialog disables and clears Exclusive for an unscoped name. The defect is only when the final name is scoped again and Exclusive isn't restored, which is a separate entry.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only reports where the label's final saved name has no scope. Reports where the final name is scoped but Exclusive was still lost belong to 'Exclusive isn't restored when an edited label name gets its scope back'.
